heading: AI integration
text: Bloom publishes its API in forms coding agents can read, so they use methods that exist instead of plausible-sounding ones that do not.

heading: Using the skill
text: Copy .claude/skills/bloom/ from the Bloom repository into your plugin project's .claude/skills/ . Claude Code then loads it when you ask for Bloom work. The skill tells the agent to: 1. Find the Minecraft versions your plugin targets and pick dependencies accordingly. 2. Read the Bloom version in your build and check the API manifest for that version instead of assuming the latest. 3. Only call methods that appear in the manifest. 4. Check capabilities before version-specific features and explain fallbacks. 5. Build with Gradle and read Bloom's startup banner when debugging. For Codex, OpenCod

heading: Asking good questions
text: Tell the agent your target versions "Spigot 1.8.8 and Paper 1.21.11" and the Bloom version. Agents cannot know whether your servers are legacy or modern otherwise, and that choice changes the build setup.

heading: Layers
text: - bloom-api holds the contracts: platform model, capabilities, scheduler interfaces, text types and utilities. It has no dependencies. - bloom-bukkit is the runtime for Bukkit-family servers: Bloom , detection, the adapter interfaces, the scheduler, messages and events. - Feature modules bloom-items , bloom-gui build on it. bloom-config and bloom-storage do not depend on Bukkit at all. - Adapters contain every piece of version-specific code.

heading: Startup
text: When you call Bloom.enable this : 1. Detect. Bloom reads the server name and version strings and probes a few classes to tell CraftBukkit, Spigot, PaperSpigot, Paper, Paper forks and Folia apart. 2. Decide. A single policy class decides whether this server is supported and which adapter family serves it. If not supported, Bloom throws BloomStartupException with the reason and what to do. 3. Load. Bloom loads the chosen adapter class by name. The name is derived from Bloom's own runtime package, so it still works after you relocate Bloom. The other adapter is never touched, which matters becaus

heading: Shutdown
text: bloom.shutdown closes everything in reverse order of creation: feature services first open menus close, databases finish queued work , then event subscriptions, then scheduled tasks, then the adapter. Errors while closing are logged and do not stop the rest. Bloom does not shut itself down on PluginDisableEvent , because Bukkit fires that event before your onDisable runs, and you may still need Bloom there to save data. Call bloom.shutdown at the end of onDisable .

heading: One jar, many APIs
text: Shared code is compiled once against spigot-api 1.8.8 and may only use Bukkit members whose binary shape is the same on every supported server. These differences are handled by adapters instead: Difference Where it bites --- --- Bukkit.getOnlinePlayers returns an array on 1.7.10, a collection later 1.7.10 InventoryView is a class before 1.21 and an interface after 1.21+ ItemMeta.spigot does not exist on modern Paper 1.21+ ItemFlag does not exist on 1.7.10 1.7.10 Materials were renamed and data values removed in 1.13 everywhere Inventory titles longer than 32 characters throw 1.7, 1.8

heading: Threads
text: - Players, worlds and inventories are touched only on the main thread. APIs that need it check and throw with an explanation, for example Menus.open and MenuView.refresh . - Storage runs on its own bounded pool; results come back as CompletableFuture s you move to the main thread with scheduler .mainThreadExecutor . - Navigation from inside menu click handlers is deferred to the next tick.

heading: Identifying items
text: Custom items are recognised by a namespaced value in the item's persistent data, never by name or lore: PersistentDataContainer on Paper, an NBT compound named BloomData on 1.7 and 1.8. Values written on one family are not readable on the other; servers do not switch families, so Bloom does not bridge them.

heading: Versions
text: Bloom uses these levels and never mixes them up: - Supported : Bloom starts and selects an adapter. - Compile-verified : the adapter's source compiled against that exact API version. - Tested on MockBukkit : Bloom's integration suite ran against MockBukkit's implementation of that API. - Tested on a real server : the self-test plugin ran on that server build and passed scripts/realserver . PaperSpigot 1.7.10 and 1.8.8 and Paper 1.21.11 and 26.3 have this status.

heading: Capabilities
text: Some features only exist on some servers. Bloom reports them as capabilities: "Probed" means the adapter checks at startup whether the feature works on this exact server build. The result is printed in the startup banner and available at runtime:

heading: What happens when a feature is missing
text: API Without the capability --- --- Messenger.actionBar , Messenger.title Follows the unsupported feature policy /docs/messaging unsupported-features : skip with one warning default , chat fallback, or throw Messenger.bossBar Returns a bar whose isFunctional is false, or throws with THROW ItemBuilder.customModelData , .unbreakable , .flags Skipped with one warning, or throws with THROW Items.setData , custom items Throws UnsupportedCapabilityException : identification must not silently fail Menu titles over 32 characters on 1.7/1.8 Truncated with one warning

heading: Java
text: Artifact Bytecode Needs --- --- --- Every module except bloom-modern Java 8 Java 8+ bloom-modern Java 21 Java 21+ Paper 26.x itself needs Java 25 Java 8 compatibility is checked by running the test suites of bloom-api , bloom-common , bloom-config , bloom-storage and bloom-testing on a real Java 8 runtime, not just by compiling for it.

heading: Newer Paper versions
text: Paper versions newer than 26.3.x are refused by default. If you test your plugin on a newer version yourself, you can opt in: Bloom logs a warning on every start in this mode.

heading: Not supported
text: - 1.9 to 1.21.0 : no adapter. Adding one is possible without changing the API. - Spigot or CraftBukkit 1.21+ : the modern adapter needs Paper's Adventure API. - Folia : its region threads need a different scheduler design.

heading: Configuration
text: bloom-config reads and writes YAML with its own SnakeYAML copy, so it behaves the same on every server. It has no Bukkit dependency.

heading: Loading a file
text: If the file does not exist, Bloom copies your bundled config.yml byte for byte , so your comments and layout reach the server owner unchanged.

heading: Reading values
text: A value missing from the file falls back to the bundled default. Getters without a fallback argument throw if the value is missing everywhere. When a section exists in the file, keys returns only the file's keys, so a kit a server owner deleted does not come back from the defaults. Mistakes in the file produce messages that point at the line:

heading: Mapping to classes
text: Fields map to kebab-case keys maxHomes becomes max-homes unless @ConfigKey says otherwise. Missing keys keep the field's default value. Supported field types: strings, numbers, booleans, characters, enums case-insensitive , UUID , Duration , List , Set , Map , nested classes with a no-argument constructor, and anything with a registered serializer.

heading: Validation
text: All problems are reported at once, each with its line, so a server owner can fix everything in one edit.

heading: Migrations
text: Before migrating, Bloom copies the file to config.yml.v1. .bak . If a migration throws, the file is left untouched. A file with a higher version than your plugin understands is refused rather than downgraded.

heading: Reloading
text: reload swaps in the new values only if the whole file loads and migrates successfully.

heading: Saving
text: save edits the file's YAML structure instead of rewriting it from scratch: comments, blank lines and the formatting of untouched values stay as the server owner left them. The write is atomic a temporary file replaces the original , so a crash never leaves half a file. Comments attached to keys that a migration moves or removes are dropped with that key; the file's header comment is always kept.

heading: New settings in updates
text: .addMissingDefaults true writes settings that exist in your bundled defaults but not in the server's file, with their comments, after backing the file up. It is off by default; values that are only missing are read from the defaults anyway.

heading: Safety
text: Values are loaded with SnakeYAML's safe constructor no arbitrary Java objects , duplicate keys are rejected, and alias expansion is limited to block "billion laughs" files.

heading: Embedded (supported)
text: Each plugin shades its own copy of Bloom and relocates it into its own package. Two plugins on one server can use different Bloom versions without conflict, and server owners install nothing extra. At startup Bloom checks how it was loaded. If its classes came from another plugin's class loader, it logs a warning: that happens when a plugin shades Bloom without relocating it, and another plugin then picks up those classes. With BloomOptions.debug true Bloom also tells you when your own copy is not relocated.

heading: Check your jar with bloom-doctor
text: bloom-doctor inspects the jar you are about to ship, before a server does: - plugin.yml exists and its main class is in the jar; - Bloom, SnakeYAML, HikariCP and SLF4J are relocated, and the Bukkit API is not bundled; - at least one platform adapter is included and which server families that covers ; - the bytecode level fits the oldest server you target Java 8 for 1.7.10 – 1.8.9 ; - with API jars given, every Bukkit/Paper method, field and class your jar uses exists with the same shape on each target server. This is what catches NoSuchMethodError , NoSuchFieldError and IncompatibleClassChange

heading: Standalone runtime (planned)
text: A Bloom plugin that others depend on, instead of shading, is on the roadmap. It needs version negotiation between plugins and a lifecycle that survives individual plugins reloading. It will not be offered until both exist and are tested; until then, embed Bloom.

heading: Licensing
text: Bloom is MIT licensed. You can embed it in closed-source and commercial plugins; keep the license notice, for example in your jar's META-INF or your documentation.

heading: Events
text: bloom.events registers listeners that belong to your plugin and are removed by bloom.shutdown . You can still use ordinary @EventHandler listeners alongside it.

heading: Lambda subscriptions
text: The handler runs at NORMAL priority and also receives cancelled events. Subscribe to concrete events such as PlayerJoinEvent ; abstract ones such as PlayerEvent have no handler list and are rejected with an explanation.

heading: Priority, filters and limits
text: - priority ... takes Bukkit's EventPriority . - ignoreCancelled skips events another listener already cancelled. - filter ... can be called several times; all filters must pass. - limit n unsubscribes after n handled events, which suits one-off reactions.

heading: Threads and errors
text: Handlers run on the thread that fires the event: the main thread for most events, a background thread for asynchronous events such as AsyncPlayerPreLoginEvent . Exceptions are reported by the server with your plugin's name, exactly like exceptions from @EventHandler methods.

heading: Menus
text: Menus come from bloom-gui . You describe a Menu once and open it for any number of players; each player gets their own MenuView with its own page and state. Menus.of bloom registers the listeners the first time you use it.

heading: A first menu
text: Slots are numbered from 0, left to right, top to bottom. button row, column, button is also available. fill ... puts a button into every slot that ends up empty.

heading: Layouts
text: Describe the menu as rows of nine characters and bind characters to buttons. Spaces are empty slots; an unbound character is an error that names the row and column.

heading: Buttons
text: - Button.of item is a decoration; Button.of item, handler is clickable. - Button.dynamic view - item computes the item on every render for that viewer. - permission node hides the button from players without the permission; permission node, item shows item instead and ignores clicks. - visibleWhen condition hides the button when the condition is false. Buttons are immutable, so one button can be shared by many menus.

heading: Clicks
text: The handler receives a ClickContext : player , kind LEFT , SHIFT RIGHT , NUMBER KEY and so on , slot , view and navigation methods. Navigation open , back , close happens on the next tick, because opening or closing inventories inside a click event is unsafe on Bukkit servers. refresh updates the items immediately.

heading: Per-player state and refreshing
text: State lives as long as the player's view: it survives refreshes, page changes and returning with back , and is discarded when the player closes the menu. refreshEvery ticks re-renders the menu for every viewer while it is open, which suits timers.

heading: Pagination
text: The page source runs on every render and returns all buttons; Bloom slices them into pages. Content goes into every slot without a button, or the slots you pass to contentSlots ... . Previous and next buttons appear only when there is a page to go to. Titles can use {page} , {pages} and {player} .

heading: Navigation and history
text: Opening a menu from another Bloom menu remembers the previous one, up to 16 levels deep. Closing the inventory clears the history.

heading: Templates
text: MenuTemplates.border , MenuTemplates.fill and MenuTemplates.paged cover the common layouts.

heading: Safety
text: Bloom cancels every click and drag while one of its menus is open: clicks in the menu, clicks in the player's own inventory, shift-clicks, number-key swaps, double-click collection and drags. If another plugin un-cancels a click, Bloom cancels it again at the highest priority and logs one warning. Items can never move into or out of a Bloom menu. Button handlers run at most once per click. A double click's second event is ignored, and a short per-player debounce stops spam clicking from buying the same thing twice: On 1.7 and 1.8 the player's inventory is resent after cancelled clicks, which r

heading: Installation
text: Bloom is a library you embed in your plugin: its classes are shaded into your jar and relocated into your own package. Nothing is installed on the server. Bloom has not been released to Maven Central or GitHub Packages. Until it is, build it from source and publish it to your local Maven repository: Then add mavenLocal to your plugin's repositories.

heading: Choose your target
text: Bloom's modules are Java 8 bytecode except bloom-modern , which is Java 21. What you compile against decides which servers your jar can run on. Compile against spigot-api 1.8.8 as Java 8 bytecode and include both adapters . This is the setup the examples use. It is verified by building the standalone template in bloom-examples/template : The same as cross-version, without bloom-modern and without disableAutoTargetJvm : Compile against paper-api with Java 21 and include only bloom-modern . You can then use Paper APIs directly in your own code:

heading: Pick modules
text: Depend only on what you use; feature modules bring the core with them. You need Add --- --- Messages, scheduler, events bloom-bukkit Items bloom-items Menus includes items bloom-gui YAML configuration bloom-config SQL storage bloom-storage Unit-test helpers bloom-testing test scope

heading: Relocate Bloom
text: Every plugin that embeds Bloom must relocate it, so two plugins with different Bloom versions never share classes. Patterns must end with a dot, otherwise io.github.crownalonedev.bloom would also match your own package if it happens to start the same way. Do not call minimize on the shadow jar. Bloom loads its adapters by name at runtime, so a minimizer cannot see that they are used and removes them. Bloom then fails to start with "the Bloom modern adapter is missing".

heading: Why disableAutoTargetJvm
text: Gradle refuses to add a Java 21 library to a Java 8 project by default. Cross-version plugins need java { disableAutoTargetJvm } because bloom-modern is Java 21 bytecode. This is safe: Bloom loads that adapter only on Paper servers, which require Java 21 or newer.

heading: Your first class
text: Build with ./gradlew shadowJar and copy build/libs/ .jar into the server's plugins folder. The console shows a line like Bloom 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT · Paper 1.21.11 Java 21.0.5 · adapter: modern .

heading: Standalone runtime (planned)
text: A shared Bloom runtime plugin that other plugins depend on is planned but not available. Embedding, as described above, is the only supported distribution today. See Distribution /docs/distribution .

heading: Introduction
text: Bloom is a Java framework for Minecraft plugins on Bukkit-family servers. It gives you one API for the things almost every plugin needs, and runs the same plugin on two very different generations of Minecraft: - Legacy : Bukkit, Spigot and PaperSpigot 1.7.10 to 1.8.9 on Java 8, the home of most PvP and HCF servers. - Modern : Paper 1.21.1 to 1.21.11 on Java 21 and 26.1 to 26.3.x on Java 25. Between them, Bukkit's API changed in ways that break compiled plugins: methods changed return types, classes became interfaces, materials were renamed and text moved to components. Bloom compiles your plug

heading: What you get
text: Area Module Highlights --- --- --- Core bloom-bukkit One-line startup, platform detection, scheduler, messages, events Menus bloom-gui Layouts, pagination, back navigation, confirmation dialogs, duplication-safe clicks Items bloom-items Modern material names everywhere, persistent custom item ids, serialization Configuration bloom-config Defaults, typed getters, validation with line numbers, migrations, comment-safe saves Storage bloom-storage SQLite, MySQL and MariaDB off the main thread, transactions, migrations Testing bloom-testing A tick-by-tick scheduler and a controllable clock

heading: How Bloom thinks about versions
text: Bloom never pretends. If a server has no adapter, Bloom refuses to start and explains why. If a server lacks a feature boss bars on 1.8, for example , Bloom reports it as a missing capability you can check, and each API documents what happens instead. Bloom is pre-release software. Its self-test plugin passes on real PaperSpigot 1.7.10 and 1.8.8 and Paper 1.21.11 and 26.3 servers; the modern adapter is also tested on MockBukkit and compiles against Paper 1.21.1, 1.21.11 and 26.3. See Compatibility /docs/compatibility for exactly what has been verified.

heading: Where to go next
text: - New to Bloom: follow the Quickstart /docs/quickstart . - Setting up a build: Installation /docs/installation covers legacy, modern and cross-version plugins. - Curious about the design: read Architecture /docs/architecture . - Using an AI coding agent: see AI integration /docs/ai-integration .

heading: Items
text: Items.of bloom returns the item service. It needs the bloom-items module.

heading: Building items
text: Names and lore use the plugin's text format see Messaging /docs/messaging formats and render white and non-italic unless you colour them, on every version. enchant accepts modern keys sharpness and legacy Bukkit names DAMAGE ALL ; enchantments a server does not know are skipped with a warning. Method Needs --- --- name , lore , addLore , amount , enchant , glow , placeholders , format , meta nothing flags ITEM FLAGS 1.8+ unbreakable UNBREAKABLE ITEMS customModelData CUSTOM MODEL DATA modern data , customId PERSISTENT DATA CONTAINER or ITEM NBT TAGS glow uses the native enchantment glint on mod

heading: Material names
text: Write modern 1.13+ names everywhere. On legacy servers Bloom maps them to the old material and data value with a built-in table of more than 200 entries: coloured wool, glass, terracotta and carpet, dyes, woods, stone variants, flowers, heads, fish and renamed items. Legacy names and NAME:DATA are accepted too. Ambiguous names follow their modern meaning on every server: MELON is the block MELON BLOCK on 1.8 and MAP is the empty map. Potions, spawn eggs and banners changed how they store their type and are not mapped; build them with meta ... for each version you support.

heading: Custom items
text: Custom ids live in the item's persistent data under your plugin's namespace its lowercase name , so items keep them when renamed in an anvil, stored in chests or carried across restarts. Ids use lowercase letters, digits, . , and - .

heading: Item data
text: All data methods return a copy ; the original stack is unchanged. Modern Paper stores data in the PersistentDataContainer . Legacy servers store it in an NBT compound called BloomData , written through reflection that is probed at startup ITEM NBT TAGS . Data written on one family is not readable on the other.

heading: Serialization
text: Use this to keep items in a database or config. The format depends on the platform family Paper's byte format on modern servers, Bukkit object streams on legacy servers , and items cannot move between the two families.

heading: Messaging
text: bloom.messages returns a Messenger . Messengers are immutable: withPrefix , withFormat and withUnsupportedPolicy return new ones, so keep the variants you use as fields.

heading: Sending messages
text: send adds the messenger's prefix; action bars, titles and boss bars never get the prefix. broadcast sends to every online player and the console.

heading: Placeholders
text: Write {name} in a template and pass Placeholder.of "name", value . Substitution happens in one pass, so a value that itself contains {other} is not expanded again. Unknown placeholders are left as they are. Placeholder values are plain text by default : colour codes or MiniMessage tags inside them are neutralised. That makes it safe to insert player names and chat. Use Placeholder.formatted only for text you trust.

heading: Formats
text: Bloom supports two markup formats on every server. The default is TextFormat.LEGACY ; change it for the whole plugin with BloomOptions.textFormat ... or per messenger with withFormat . LEGACY MINIMESSAGE --- --- --- Example &dHello &lworld Hello world Paper 1.21+ / 26.x Converted with Adventure, & RRGGBB hex supported Real MiniMessage 1.7 / 1.8 Native Converted by Bloom see below Bloom converts a documented subset to legacy colours: named colours, , hex colours mapped to the nearest of the 16 legacy colours, keeping saturated colours chromatic , all decorations and their negation, closing tags

heading: Action bars and titles
text: Title timings need the TITLE TIMINGS capability; on 1.8 the client's default timings are used.

heading: Boss bars
text: Boss bars exist only on modern Paper BOSS BAR . They must be created and changed on the main thread, and Bloom hides them from all viewers on shutdown.

heading: Unsupported features
text: When a server lacks a feature, the messenger's UnsupportedFeaturePolicy decides what happens: Policy Effect --- --- SKIP default Nothing is sent; the method returns false ; one warning per feature is logged FALLBACK TO CHAT Action bars and titles are sent as chat messages; boss bars are skipped THROW UnsupportedCapabilityException naming the capability and the platform

heading: Threads
text: Chat, action bars and titles can be sent from any thread. Boss bars are main-thread only. For strings that must be plain legacy text scoreboards, signs , use messenger.legacy template, placeholders... .

heading: From plain Bukkit code
text: Bloom does not replace Bukkit: your plugin still extends JavaPlugin and uses Bukkit types such as Player and ItemStack . Move one area at a time. You have Replace with --- --- Bukkit.getScheduler .runTaskLater ... bloom.scheduler .syncLater ... ; cancelled automatically getServer .getPluginManager .registerEvents ... bloom.events .register ... or subscribe ... ChatColor.translateAlternateColorCodes '&', ... + string concatenation bloom.messages .send player, template, Placeholder.of ... NMS packets for action bars and titles messages.actionBar ... , messages.title ... new ItemStack Material.WO

heading: Between Bloom versions
text: Bloom is pre-1.0: minor versions may change APIs, and every change is listed in the changelog /changelog . From 1.0, Bloom follows semantic versioning: breaking changes only in major versions, deprecations at least one minor version before removal. Data formats are treated as compatibility promises: config files migrate with backups, database schemas migrate with history, and item ids and data keep their storage format.

heading: Modules
text: All artifacts share the Maven group io.github.crownalonedev.bloom and one version. Artifact Contains Depends on Bytecode --- --- --- --- bloom-api Platform model, capabilities, scheduler and service interfaces, Placeholder , Cooldowns , Durations , ExpiringCache nothing Java 8 bloom-bukkit Bloom , BloomOptions , Messenger , Events , adapter interfaces bloom-api Java 8 bloom-items Items , ItemBuilder , CustomItem , MaterialMappings bloom-bukkit Java 8 bloom-gui Menus , Menu , Button , ConfirmMenu , MenuTemplates bloom-items Java 8 bloom-config YamlConfig , validation, migrations, TypeSerializer

heading: Adapters are runtime-only
text: Your code never references adapter classes; Bloom finds them by name. Declare them with runtimeOnly so they are shaded into your jar but stay out of your compile classpath.

heading: Third-party libraries
text: - SnakeYAML 2.7 with bloom-config . Servers bundle different, incompatible SnakeYAML versions, so Bloom brings its own. Relocate org.yaml.snakeyaml. . - HikariCP 4.0.3 and SLF4J API with bloom-storage . HikariCP 4 is the last line that runs on Java 8; its API is compatible with newer versions if your plugin is modern-only. Relocate com.zaxxer.hikari. and org.slf4j. . Hikari's own log output is silent unless you add an SLF4J binding. - JDBC drivers are not bundled. Servers ship SQLite and MySQL drivers; shade MariaDB's driver yourself.

heading: Logging
text: Bloom logs through your plugin's logger java.util.logging , so messages appear under your plugin's name on every server without extra libraries.

heading: Quickstart
text: This walk-through builds the plugin from the homepage: a shop menu that feeds the player, opened when they join. It assumes you completed Installation /docs/installation with bloom-gui and both adapters.

heading: 1. Enable Bloom
text: Bloom.enable this detects the server, picks the adapter and starts Bloom's services. bloom.shutdown stops everything Bloom started for your plugin, in order. Always pair them.

heading: 2. Build an item and a menu
text: Items use modern material names on every server. On 1.8, COOKED BEEF stays the same and names that changed in 1.13, such as LIME WOOL , are mapped to their legacy material and data value automatically. A few things happen for you here: - The menu cancels every click and drag, so the item can never be taken out. - click.close waits until the next tick, which is the safe moment to close an inventory. - actionBar shows an action bar on servers that have one and is skipped, with one console warning, on 1.7.10. - The join listener and the delayed task are removed when the plugin disables.

heading: 3. Build and run
text: Put the jar from build/libs into a test server's plugins folder and join. The startup log tells you which adapter Bloom chose and which capabilities the server has.

heading: Next steps
text: - Menus /docs/gui : layouts, pagination and navigation. - Items /docs/items : custom items that survive renames and server restarts. - Configuration /docs/configuration : let server owners change prices and titles. - Storage /docs/storage : keep player data in SQLite or MySQL.

heading: Scheduling
text: bloom.scheduler returns a BloomScheduler . Every task belongs to your plugin and is cancelled by bloom.shutdown . If a task throws, the exception is logged with your plugin's name and other tasks keep running.

heading: Main-thread tasks
text: Use sync methods for anything that touches players, worlds, entities or inventories. Delays and periods are in ticks 20 per second or Duration s, which are rounded up to whole ticks. A delay of zero means the next tick, as in Bukkit.

heading: Repeating tasks that stop themselves
text: Repeating tasks receive their own handle, so they can cancel themselves without a field:

heading: Background work
text: async methods run on background threads. Use them for files, web requests and heavy computation, then come back to the main thread before touching the game: Never modify worlds, entities or inventories from an async task. Bukkit is not thread-safe, and such bugs show up as rare crashes or corrupted chunks, long after the code was written.

heading: Thread checks
text: Bloom's own main-thread APIs menus, boss bars perform this check for you.

heading: Reference
text: Method Runs on Notes --- --- --- sync Runnable main next tick syncLater Runnable, ticks or Duration main syncRepeating Consumer , delay, period main period at least one tick async Runnable / asyncLater / asyncRepeating background supplySync Supplier / supplyAsync Supplier main / background returns CompletableFuture ; cancelled futures fail with CancellationException on shutdown mainThreadExecutor / asyncExecutor main / background for CompletableFuture chains activeTaskCount tasks not yet finished or cancelled Folia is not supported yet, because its region threads do not fit a single main threa

heading: Storage
text: bloom-storage runs SQL on its own threads and hands you CompletableFuture s. It does not depend on Bukkit, and it is not an ORM: you write SQL, Bloom takes care of connections, threads, parameters and shutdown.

heading: Opening a database
text: SQLite uses one connection by default, which serialises writes and avoids "database is locked" errors, plus WAL mode, foreign keys and a busy timeout. For MySQL: Bloom picks the JDBC driver the server provides: SQLite and MySQL drivers ship with Spigot and Paper on 1.8, Bloom falls back to the old com.mysql.jdbc.Driver . MariaDB's driver must be shaded into your plugin. If the database is unreachable, build fails immediately with the address and a hint. Use a different migrationTable per plugin when several plugins share one MySQL database.

heading: Migrations
text: Applied versions are recorded in the history table, and each migration runs in its own transaction. MySQL and MariaDB commit schema changes immediately, so keep each migration to one logical change. If the database has a newer version than your plugin's migrations, migrate fails instead of continuing with an unknown schema.

heading: Queries
text: Results arrive on a database thread. Switch to the main thread with mainThreadExecutor before touching players. Parameters are bound in order. Besides strings, numbers and booleans you can pass UUID stored as text , enums stored by name , Instant epoch milliseconds , Duration milliseconds , byte and null . Method Returns --- --- update sql, params... rows affected insert sql, params... generated key, if any batch sql, rows rows affected per parameter row query sql, mapper, params... all rows queryOne sql, mapper, params... first row, or empty

heading: Transactions
text: The transaction commits when the callback returns and rolls back when it throws. Use inTransaction tx - ... when there is no result. The Transaction object is only valid inside the callback.

heading: Repositories
text: SqlRepository generates find , findAll , save an upsert and delete . Table and column names are validated as plain identifiers. On SQLite the upsert is INSERT OR REPLACE , which works on the old SQLite bundled with 1.8 servers but deletes and re-inserts the row, so ON DELETE CASCADE children are removed; MySQL uses ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE .

heading: Blocking calls off the main thread
text: db.blocking throws IllegalStateException when called on the main thread, as reported by mainThreadCheck .

heading: Limits and shutdown
text: - Operations wait in a bounded queue 1,000 by default, queueCapacity . When it is full, new operations fail at once with "The database queue is full" instead of piling up memory while the database is down. - close stops accepting work, waits for queued operations 10 seconds by default, shutdownTimeout , fails anything that could not run, and closes the pool. Register the database as a Bloom service and Bloom does this on shutdown. - Error messages include the SQL statement but never parameter values, which may contain personal data. SQLite is tested by Bloom's build on Java 8 and Java 21, and

heading: Unit tests without a server
text: Write game logic against BloomScheduler and Clock instead of Bukkit's scheduler and System.currentTimeMillis , then drive time yourself with bloom-testing : ManualScheduler runs nothing until you call tick . "Async" tasks also run during ticks, on the test thread, so tests need no sleeps. It shares the real scheduler's cancellation and error handling. TestClock does the same for Cooldowns and ExpiringCache .

heading: MockBukkit
text: For modern Paper behaviour you can test with MockBukkit https://mockbukkit.org : Bloom detects it and loads the modern adapter. MockBukkit only exists for modern Paper; there is no maintained mock for 1.8. MockBukkit reports features it has not implemented as skipped tests, not failures. Check skip counts, or fail the build on skips as Bloom's own integration tests do; otherwise untested code looks tested.

heading: How Bloom is tested
text: - Unit tests for every module; the server-independent modules also run on a real Java 8 runtime. - MockBukkit integration tests that load the real modern adapter, plus every example plugin's shaded and relocated jar. - Compile checks of the modern adapter against Paper 1.21.1, 1.21.11 and 26.3. - SQLite tests on the old sqlite-jdbc 3.7.2 driver, and MySQL 8.4 / MariaDB 11 tests in CI. - bloom-doctor linkage checks of every example plugin against spigot-api 1.8.8 and paper-api 1.21.11 and 26.3. - A real-server harness, scripts/realserver/run.sh run.bat on Windows , which downloads an official P

heading: "cannot run on ... is not supported"
text: The server version has no adapter. The message lists the supported ranges. Common cases: - 1.9 to 1.21.0 : not supported. Use 1.8.x or Paper 1.21.1+. - Spigot 1.21+ : run Paper instead; the modern adapter needs Paper's API. - Newer than 26.3.x : update Bloom, or opt in with allowNewerUntestedVersions true after testing yourself. - Folia : not supported yet.

heading: "needs the Bloom modern adapter, but it is not in the plugin jar"
text: Add runtimeOnly "io.github.crownalonedev.bloom:bloom-modern:..." or bloom-legacy and make sure the shadow jar contains it. If you use minimize , remove it: minimizers cannot see that adapters are loaded by name.

heading: "Bloom is already running for plugin X"
text: Either Bloom.enable was called twice without shutdown , or two plugins shade Bloom without relocating it and share its classes. Relocate Bloom in every plugin that embeds it.

heading: "was compiled for a newer Java version"
text: The modern adapter needs Java 21. This message on a 1.21+ server means the server runs on an older Java than Paper requires.

heading: "Dependency resolution is looking for a library compatible with JVM runtime version 8"
text: Your plugin targets Java 8 and depends on bloom-modern Java 21 . Add java { disableAutoTargetJvm } . See Installation /docs/installation why-disableautotargetjvm .

heading: My own classes were relocated
text: A relocation pattern without a trailing dot matches every package that starts with the same text. Use relocate "io.github.crownalonedev.bloom.", ".../libs/bloom." with the trailing dots.

heading: NoSuchMethodError or IncompatibleClassChangeError on one server version
text: Your own code called a Bukkit method whose signature differs between versions, for example Bukkit.getOnlinePlayers array on 1.7.10 or a method on InventoryView class before 1.21, interface after . Use Bloom's adapter bloom.adapter .players .onlinePlayers , or compile against the oldest API you support.

heading: Debug output
text: Debug mode logs the result of each legacy feature probe and relocation details.

heading: Utilities
text: These live in bloom-api and need no server.

heading: Cooldowns
text: tryUse is atomic per key, so two quick clicks cannot both pass. Expired entries are removed when touched and by prune ; call it from a repeating task if many keys are never touched again. Cooldowns are kept in memory only.

heading: Durations
text: Units: ms , s , m , h , d , w . A bare number means seconds. Invalid input throws an exception whose message lists valid examples, which you can show to the player directly.

heading: Expiring cache
text: A least-recently-used cache with a time-to-live and a size limit. It uses one lock, so it suits modest caches; for very hot paths, use a dedicated caching library.

heading: Ticks
text: Ticks.from Duration rounds up to whole ticks, so a positive duration never becomes zero. Ticks.toDuration long and Ticks.seconds long convert the other way.
